question: Do the guardrails we set by intuition — per-subsection caps and per-section format prescription — hold up on REAL template sections and narrative content?
method: Second fixture (scripts/eval/fixtures/golden-facts-anchoring.md, 19 facts) chosen as a contrast to the gate fixture: mechanism narrative (a five-step algorithm with tie-breaks) rather than enumerable rules. Writers are fresh-context subagents reading only pkg/comment/anchor.go; judges are fresh-context and read the fact list, never the writers' prompts.

pooled_vs_per_subsection_caps.conditions: Findings section, 600-word section cap. POOLED = section cap only. PERSUB = section cap + 150 words per finding. Two runs each, 4-6 findings required.
pooled_vs_per_subsection_caps.verdict: NULL RESULT, honestly reported — the per-finding cap never bound (largest finding 135 vs the 150 cap), so the cannibalization it exists to prevent never occurred. Pooled drafts self-balanced.
findings: No cannibalization at this pressure: every smallest finding carried real content, not padding (the thinnest, 74 words, carried a full fact plus its rationale and an actionable warning).
Facts-per-word did not track finding size; the LARGEST findings were consequence-heavy, not fact-hoarding.

Per-subsection drafts covered +2 facts on average with the only mangle appearing in a pooled draft — but with n=2 and one flat outlier, that is direction, not evidence. Plausible mechanism is completeness pressure per finding, NOT length flattening.
Design fix for a rerun: the section cap must be tight enough (or the subject rich enough) that findings actually compete — at 495-575 words against a 600 cap they never did.

format_prescription.conditions: Same subject and 250-word cap, format prescribed: bullets / semantic-line-break prose / markdown table. One run each, coverage + rubric judged.
findings: LOOKUP and NARRATIVE select DIFFERENT formats — the eval's main result. Table wins navigability 5 vs prose 2 (row+column addressing gives every rule a two-key address); prose is the only format that stated forward-looking invariants ('preserve that separation or context will stop winning'), which neither other format carried.
Bullets carried the most golden facts per word (0.072 vs 0.067 table, 0.066 prose) and scored highest on accuracy — the safe default when a section is neither pure lookup nor pure rationale.

Each format loses the content class its shape has no slot for, and the losses are DISJOINT: the table dropped definitional setup (what an Anchor even is — no Step row key for it), bullets dropped failure branches of rules already stated (the bullet's slot was full), prose dropped enumerable constants (nil returns, the 60-char truncation, the exact error string).

Format-specific mangling is real: the table's step-5 cell reads as unconditional ('nothing matched -> orphan') because a cell must be short, but the code silently keeps an anchorless in-bounds comment. The exception had nowhere to go in the grid. Prose committed the analogous sin with an unconditional 'mutates ... setting AnchorConfidence' (untouched on the orphan path).
A rationale COLUMN rescues the table: the 'Gotcha when changing' column carried change-consequences prose lacked entirely. Prescribing a table without such a column is what would lose rationale.

template_implications: Do NOT prescribe one format per section blindly. Prescribe by section PURPOSE: lookup-shaped sections (Interfaces, step tables, config) earn a table WITH a consequences column; rationale-shaped sections (Data Flow, Decisions, Risks) must stay prose or they lose the invariants; mixed sections default to bullets.
A table in a template should require a 'why / what breaks' column, and definitional setup must live outside the grid — a table cannot define its own subject.
Keep max_subsection_words, but this run did not justify it; its value remains unmeasured at realistic pressure. Do not cite this eval as evidence for the current 200-word setting.
caveats: One run per format; two per cap condition. The cap experiment is underpowered by construction (cap never bound). Writers and judges share a model family. Fixture is technical mechanism content — user-facing or decision narrative may differ again.
